mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS rises by >0.5% QoQ.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4.0% coincident with a decline in payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals labor market stress, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 4.0% AND PAYEMS falls month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) when both UNRATE > 4.0% and PAYEMS falls MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) during three-month INDPRO contraction below its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the Case-Shiller Home Price Index (not available; using HOUST as a proxy for housing activity) combined with rising mortgage spreads (not available; using RSAFS as a proxy for household savings) signals a housing demand boom that boosts consumer confidence and spending, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises >2% MoM AND RSAFS rises >1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both HOUST and RSAFS show the specified increases.

mechanism_narrative: A low and stable federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0% for 6 consecutive months) in the absence of inflationary pressure (CPIAUCSL < 2.5% YoY) signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports risk asset valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2.0% AND CPIAUCSL < 2.5% for 6 consecutive months
regime_hint: prolonged monetary accommodation with low inflation
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during 6-month periods of low and stable FEDFUNDS with low inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) during four-month periods where PAYEMS is above its 12-month MA.

mechanism_narrative: A strong acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above its 6-month moving average, accompanied by rising home sales (HOUST), signals a demand recovery in the consumer and housing sectors, which lifts corporate earnings and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.10) when both GDPC1 accelerates and HOUST rises sharply.
